01. Do you have at least 2 years of college with coursework in education, counseling, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of training and experience that demonstrates the ability to assist students academically in a college environment? Options: Yes | No
Commitment to working with students from diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, and ethnic backgrounds, including those who have previously disengaged from high school.
Experience supporting high school or college students in academic or tutoring settings.
Understanding of dual enrollment and high school re-engagement models.

Completion of two (2) years of college with coursework in education, counseling, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of training and experience that demonstrates the ability to assist students academically in a college environment.
Experience facilitating workshops or group learning sessions.
Assists in the day-to-day coordination of Gateway to College academic support, including scheduling, workshop planning, and tracking student academic progress.
Supports instructors and counselors in orienting high school students to the college environment and dual enrollment expectations.
Provides support to students with understanding assignments, time management,and navigating Canvas and other academic platforms.
Assists individuals and small groups in academic skill development in both general education and guided pathway courses.
Explains basic concepts, instructions, and resources to support student learning.
Help students use lab or classroom technology, campus solutions software if applicable.
Maintains accurate records related to attendance, tutoring sessions, and workshop participation.
Prepares and organizes instructional materials for classroom and workshop use.
Operates standard office equipment and personal computers to support instruction and student services.
Participates in Gateway to College outreach, career exploration, and dual enrollment events.
Performs other related duties as assigned.
Proficiency in using personal computers and academic platforms (Canvas, Google Workspace, Microsoft Office).
Familiarity with career pathways or CTE education (e.g., 3D fabrication, engineering, wood tech).
Organized, energetic, and adaptable to a dynamic learning environment.
Strong interpersonal communication and problem-solving skills.
Ability to maintain confidentiality, professionalism, and a student-centered approach.
